resourceProfile.assessment: The complete English and Japanese source scope, review metadata, glossary, and project concept references were available locally.

automatedQuality.summary: Translation review checks, typecheck, complete build, route and generated-link checks, and the full test suite passed after the cycle was finalized.

linguisticCritique.summary: A bounded Japanese pass identified nine remaining trigonometry and circuit-terminology defects; all nine were corrected.

competentHumanReview.summary: No competent Japanese human review was performed in this cycle; changed IDs remain machine-drafted.

publicationAuthorization.summary: No merge, publication, deployment, or residual-risk authorization was requested or granted for this cycle.

findings.summary: The Japanese right-triangle formulas retained English side labels.
evidence: The formulas used opposite, adjacent, and hypotenuse instead of 対辺, 隣辺, and 斜辺.
findings.resolution: Localized all three side labels in the formulas.

findings.summary: The inverse-trigonometry formulas retained English side labels.
evidence: The previous expressions contained opposite, adjacent, and hypotenuse.
findings.resolution: Localized the side labels while preserving inverse-function notation.

findings.summary: The worked trigonometry example retained English side labels.
evidence: The example formulas began with opposite and adjacent despite Japanese explanatory prose.
findings.resolution: Changed the labels to 対辺 and 隣辺.

findings.summary: The right-triangle section mixed Japanese prose with English formula terminology.
evidence: The paragraph used 対辺, 隣辺, and 斜辺 while all three formulas used English labels.
findings.resolution: Aligned the formula terminology with the established Japanese prose.

findings.summary: The angle-finding section was inconsistent across inverse formulas and the worked example.
evidence: The inverse formulas and example used English side labels in an otherwise Japanese section.
findings.resolution: Applied one consistent Japanese terminology set throughout the section.

findings.summary: The series-cell formula retained the English word series in a Japanese formula annotation.
evidence: The previous expression ended with (series) while the surrounding section used Japanese terms.

findings.summary: The three displayed ratios did not use the Japanese terminology established in the explanation.
evidence: Formula labels were not localized even though the explanatory sentence defined all three Japanese terms.
findings.resolution: Normalized the three displayed ratios to Japanese side terminology.

findings.summary: The inverse ratios did not match the Japanese terminology used in the preceding section.
evidence: The inverse formulas continued to expose English side names to Japanese readers.
findings.resolution: Reused 対辺, 隣辺, and 斜辺 in the inverse formulas.

findings.summary: The worked example did not match the localized Japanese labels used elsewhere in the section.
evidence: The example retained English opposite and adjacent labels.
findings.resolution: Aligned the example with the Japanese side terminology.
